endorsements.quote: Lastly, healthcare systems should continue to monitor performance periodically to ensure there has been no deterioration in model performance over time, as the model may evolve or the workflows and patient populations change.

As with any new medical device, the AI model’s performance should be assessed pre-deployment by its developer against a set of standard, industry-endorsed set of benchmarks and validated on an external data set.
That is why when physicians interpret CT perfusion images, they should always review the quality of the source images as well as the baseline non-contrast CT of the brain.6

unlisted_practices: Train AI models on datasets that include different age groups, races, ethnic groups, and social classes whenever feasible to improve generalizability and mitigate bias.
Locally validate AI models in the healthcare setting before deployment to ensure expected performance in the local workflow and patient population.
Continuously monitor AI model performance after implementation to detect deterioration over time.
Train imaging AI algorithms on large volumes of data from a variety of imaging devices and protocols.
Validate AI models across populations and geographic areas to strengthen generalizability.
Use privacy-preserving approaches such as federated learning or honest brokers independent of the AI research team for linking data to train AI models.
Base AI-assisted patient recruitment for trials on fixed, pre-set criteria.

screen.reason: This is a workshop consensus/recommendations paper from the Stroke Treatment Academic Industry Roundtable discussing opportunities, challenges, and recommendations for incorporating AI and novel trial designs in acute stroke research and clinical practice.
